title: Where Has the Foreign Signal Gone?
abstract: arXiv:2610.28175v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: We compare the relation between sentiment noise in the Twitter feed and losses for stocks of domestic and foreign firms. The mean quarterly domestic-foreign difference in the slope of next-quarter losses on measured noise is -1.40 (Newey-West t = -2.99). This slope is negative for 78 and 48 percent of the quarters for domestic and foreign stocks, respectively (block-bootstrap p = 0.016). Thus, this relationship is temporally more stable for domestic stocks. We use a noisy rational expectations model to explain these patterns through the composition of the contributor pool. The feeds for stocks of foreign firms have higher repeat-author concentration and a larger model-implied nonfundamental component than those for domestic firms. We interpret these differences through the producer-knowledge mismatch hypothesis. translated_abstract: 我们比较了Twitter信息流中的情绪噪声与本国公司及外国公司股票损失之间的关系。下一季度损失对所测噪声的斜率的季度均值“国内-国外”差异为-1.40（Newey-West t = -2.99）。对于本国股票和外国股票，该斜率分别在78%和48%的季度中为负（块自助法 p = 0.016）。因此，这一关系在时间上对本国股票更加稳定。我们运用一个噪声理性预期模型，通过贡献者池的构成来解释这些模式。与本国公司相比，外国公司股票的信息流具有更高的重复作者集中度，以及更大的模型隐含的非基本面成分。我们通过“生产者-知识错配假说”来解读这些差异：对于外国公司，英语贡献者池低估了往往拥有信息优势的母国市场投资者……（原文摘要至此截断）
tldr: 该研究发现Twitter情绪噪声对下一季度股票损失的预测关系在本国股票上比外国股票更加稳定，并用“生产者-知识错配假说”解释：外国股票的英语Twitter贡献者池缺乏拥有信息的母国市场投资者，导致其信息流中非基本面噪声成分更大。
en_tdlr: The study finds that the relation between Twitter sentiment noise and next-quarter stock losses is temporally more stable for domestic stocks than for foreign stocks, and explains this via a producer-knowledge mismatch hypothesis: the English-language Twitter contributor pool for foreign firms underrepresents home-market investors, leading to a larger nonfundamental noise component in foreign stocks' feeds.
